holidays.name: Library Lovers' Day
holidays.description: A day for book nerds to skip the roses and show some love to their local library, from the dusty stacks to the heroic librarians who know where everything is hiding.
holidays.origin: Library Lovers' Day began in the early 2000s as a grassroots observance in the library community, designed to piggyback on Valentine's Day by encouraging people to celebrate their love of libraries and reading.
holidays.funFact: The Library of Congress holds over 170 million items, which means you could in theory fall in love with a different one every day for a very, very long time.

holidays.name: Ferris Wheel Day
holidays.description: A spinning celebration of the giant, slow, scenic carnival ride that lets you dangle high above the ground while pretending you are totally not afraid of heights.
holidays.origin: It is celebrated on the birthday of George Washington Gale Ferris Jr., born February 14, 1859, who designed the first Ferris Wheel for the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago.
holidays.funFact: The original Ferris Wheel stood about 264 feet tall and carried up to 2,160 passengers at once in 36 cars, each roughly the size of a bus.

holidays.name: Race Relations Day
holidays.description: Not so much a quirky party as a thoughtful pause, this observance encourages people to talk, listen, and build understanding across racial lines.
holidays.origin: Race Relations Day was started in the early 20th century by Americans in the interfaith and civil rights community who wanted a day dedicated to improving relationships between races. It was later popularized by church groups.
holidays.funFact: It originally fell on the second Sunday in February, and it was partly timed to coincide with the birthdays of Abraham Lincoln and Frederick Douglass, who is traditionally said to have celebrated his on February 14.

holidays.name: Organ Donor Day
holidays.description: While everyone else is giving chocolates and cards, this day encourages people to give a bit more by signing up to be an organ donor, proving that the most meaningful gift literally comes from the heart.
holidays.origin: National Donor Day was started in 1998 by Saint Barnabas Health Care System, the Gift of Life Donor Program, and others, and was timed to coincide with Valentine's Day for its heart-related theme.
holidays.funFact: A single organ donor can save up to eight lives, which makes them far better at romance than a box of drugstore chocolates.

holidays.name: Call in Single Day
holidays.description: A cheeky counter-holiday in which single people are encouraged to take a day off from work to treat themselves, because couples shouldn't be the only ones having fun on Valentine's Day.
holidays.origin: This tongue-in-cheek observance sprang up in internet culture as a humorous alternative to Valentine's Day, modeled on the idea of calling in sick but with a relationship-status twist.
holidays.funFact: It is part of a broader trend of anti-Valentine's celebrations, including Singles Awareness Day, which people casually abbreviate as S.A.D., a fittingly self-aware acronym.
